newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close broadly higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close broadly higher.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed broadly higher on Sunday in thin trading, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.11 pct to 104.85
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.11 to 103.84
Volume, mostly concentrated in the Makam and unlinked bonds, was a low 126 million shekels.

"Despite the fact that trading opened with high demand volume remained relatively low. The market rose across the board with yields on CPI-linked bonds falling to only 4.15 percent," said a trader at Evergreen Capital Markets.
"Yields on these bonds are expected to stabilise at the short term before falling further below four percent," he said.
Gidi Halperin, investment manager at Meitav Investments and Securities, said he believes that in the long run yields on inflation-linked bonds would continue to decline to 3.8 percent or even lower.

"There are different forces working at the market. On the one hand, there are investors who fear that inflation would rise. These investors protect themselves by buying CPI-linked bonds," Halperin said.
"Others believe that inflation is under control and will be relatively lower at around 9-9.5 percent in 1997. These investors prefer the unlinked bonds and Makams," he said.
The Evergreen trader said the market will remain stable at the current level before it starts rising again.
Traders noted that dollar-linked bonds were Sunday's main gainers following the rise of the U.S. currency on overseas markets.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
